subject: Discovery: inference unit-econ & batching pilot — next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@cobaltanalytics.com>, Leah O'Connor <leah@cobaltanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: inference unit-econ & batching pilot — next steps

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path forward so we keep momentum. Notes are intentionally concise — tell me if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared
- Token spend is the top cost pressure: averaging ~1.4M tokens/day across search + chat routes.
- 95th pct latency spikes on small query routes (search) are causing UX drops; need sub-300ms 95th for search.
- Current infra: internal endpoints on EKS hitting Gen2 Triton cluster (FP16), no KV cache today.
- You’re open to quantization for cheaper models provided quality regressions are <5% on your internal eval set.

Success criteria for a pilot (what we heard)
- Reduce per-token inference cost by >=35% for high-volume search route while keeping quality within 5% of baseline.
- 95th percentile latency for search <= 300ms under your peak QPS.
- Clear rollout plan for production (canary -> scale) with rollback triggers.

Technical assumptions to validate
- Average request length for search: 40 tokens prompt / 30 tokens generation (please confirm).
- Peak QPS for the route: ~120 RPS with spiky bursts to 250 RPS.
- You will share a sanitized sample workload and eval prompts for us to run local cost/latency sims.

Proposed next steps (week 0 -> week 4 pilot timeline)
1) Shared artifacts: you send workload CSV + sample prompts + baseline metric export (CloudWatch/Prometheus) — due Wed 11/3.
2) Redwood runs an initial unit-econ simulation (batching + prefix caching assumptions) and shares a short MRP (2–3 slides) by Fri 11/6.
3) Tech sync (30–45m) to align pilot infra: dataset access, model variant(s), quantization tolerance — target Mon 11/9.
4) Pilot kickoff (test traffic, isolated pool) with mutual action plan and success gates — 2–3 week window after kickoff.

Attachments: I’ve attached a blank pilot scope template and an example mutual action plan.

Would you like us to propose specific model variants to test (e.g., 7B int8 vs 13B q4) or keep that until we see your sample workload?

Thanks — looking forward to the sample files.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment stubs: mutual_action_plan_COB_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot_scope_requirements.md (markdown)

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@cobaltanalytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah O'Connor <leah@cobaltanalytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T18:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: inference unit-econ & batching pilot — next steps

Thanks Tessa — solid summary. A couple clarifications and a small change to timeline: we can get a sanitized workload out but need until Friday (11/6) — there’s PII scrubbing involved.

Confirmations / notes
- Search route average tokens: your numbers are in the right ballpark; confirm exact avg after we send CSV (current best estimate: 35 prompt / 28 gen).
- Peak QPS: 100 sustained, very spiky bursts up to 220 during business hours.
- We are willing to test int8/4-bit variants but we must run automatic quality checks against our intent-preservation suite. Anything that drops intent classification accuracy >3% will be a blocker.

Change to timeline: could we shift Redwood’s simulation deliverable to Tue 11/10 (gives our security team time to sign off on dataset)?

Also attaching a small workload sample (sanitized excerpt) — file: Cobalt_MVP_workload_summary.csv.

—Samir

Attachment stubs: Cobalt_MVP_workload_summary.csv (CSV, 2MB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@cobaltanalytics.com>, Leah O'Connor <leah@cobaltanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: inference unit-econ & batching pilot — next steps

Perfect — thanks for the sample excerpt and the timeline update, Samir. We’ll shift the sim deliverable to Tue 11/10. Quick internal notes so everyone’s aligned: Aditya / Monica, please see the workload excerpt and Samir’s quality threshold (<=3% intent drop).

What we’ll run next
- Cost simulation with three knobs: batching strategies (fixed vs adaptive), prefix/KV caching assumptions (no cache vs conservative hit rate 30% vs aggressive 60%), and quantization options (FP16 baseline, int8, q4-like).
- Latency sims under your burst profile (100 RPS sustained, 220 bursts).
- Small quality sweep using Cobalt’s intent test set (we’ll run locally against sanitized prompts you provided).

Pre-kickoff ask: please confirm which S3 bucket/presigned URLs we should use for upload and whether your security team expects an encrypted transfer / additional paperwork. Also confirm a preferred tech sync slot on Mon 11/9 (I can do 9–11am PT or 2–4pm PT).

I’ll attach an updated mutual action plan after internal alignment, and we’ll propose model variants in the simulation deck.

Best,

Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime

From: Leah O'Connor <leah@cobaltanalytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@cobaltanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: inference unit-econ & batching pilot — next steps

Thanks all — quick answers from our side:
- Security: encrypted transfer preferred; we can generate presigned URLs with AES-256 server-side encryption. I’ll loop in our security engineer if Redwood needs an IP allowlist.
- Tech sync: Mon 11/9 10:00am PT works for Samir and me — please send a calendar invite.
- We accept Redwood proposing model variants, but we’ll gate final choices on the quality sweep results.

One more ask: could Redwood include a short appendix in the sim deck that quantifies the tradeoff between batching-induced latency tails and token-cost reduction? That’s a key internal decision factor for us.

Leah
Director of Product, Cobalt Analytics
leah@cobaltanalytics.com
